title: Syr Darya Lower-Delta Rice Polders
summary: Soviet planners in the 1960s–70s converted the Syr Darya's lower delta in Kazakhstan into intensive rice-growing polders, dyking off shallow lake beds and marshes. Drainage and irrigation salted the soils within two decades; the delta wetlands that once fed fisheries were desiccated. The polders were abandoned and the land is now salt crust and scrub.
